h1: The 8 Best Bluetooth Trackers Under $25 for Keys, Wallets and Bags, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Bluetooth Tracker Under $25: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 Bluetooth trackers under $25 compared on phone compatibility, find network, water resistance, battery and form factor.
summary: The second-generation Apple AirTag is the best tracker for iPhone owners, with a huge Find My network and improved Precision Finding. The Tile Pro is the best option if your household mixes iPhone and Android, the Samsung SmartTag2 is the clear choice for Galaxy owners, and the Android Find Hub four-pack is the best value for multiple items.
intro: Before comparing any tracker, answer one question: which phone do you carry? A Bluetooth tag is nearly useless on its own, because it only reports its location when another phone in the network passes close by and relays the signal. A tag tied to the wrong network for your phone is a keychain ornament, however good the hardware looks.

We ranked eight trackers priced under $25 by phone compatibility first, then by find network, water resistance, battery life and form factor. The listings give some figures, such as IP ratings and battery years, and we use only those. No tracker replaces a GPS device, and a few listings that use the word GPS deserve skepticism, which we flag where it applies.

products.name: Apple AirTag (2nd Generation): Tracker for Keychain, Wallet, and More; Locator with Sound; Simple One-Tap Setup with iPhone or iPad
products.verdict: The best tracker for iPhone, now with up to 1.5X Precision Finding range.
products.description:
The second-generation AirTag is a locator with a built-in speaker, one-tap setup with an iPhone or iPad and a listed range for Precision Finding that is up to 1.5X better than before. Precision Finding is the arrow-and-distance display that guides you straight to a lost item once you are close.

It ranks first because it taps the Find My network, which is built from a vast number of Apple devices that anonymously relay any tag they pass. In crowded places that means a lost item can appear on your map within minutes, an advantage no competitor matches on an iPhone. It is useless on Android, which is why Android owners should skip it, and it has no keyring hole, so you need a holder.

Buy it if you carry an iPhone. Skip it if anyone in your household who will use it carries Android.

keySpecs.value: One tap with iPhone or iPad

pros: Built-in sound helps you locate items
cons: Needs a separate holder for keys
products.idealFor: iPhone and iPad owners who lose keys, bags and wallets.
products.skipIf: You or your family use Android phones.

products.name: Life360 Tile Pro - Powerful Bluetooth Tracker, Key Finder and Item Locator for Keys, Bags and More. Both iOS and Android Compatible.
products.verdict: The tracker that works on iPhone and Android alike.
products.description:
The Tile Pro is the step-up Tile for keys and bags, with a tag you can ring from your phone and a design for both iOS and Android. It is part of the Life360 family, which also runs a family location app.

It ranks second because it is the only high-quality tracker here that does not care which phone you carry. A household with an iPhone and a Galaxy can share the same tags and the same app. The tradeoff is the network: Tile's community is smaller than Apple's, so a lost item far from other Tile users may stay unfound longer. Some extras also sit behind a paid plan.

Buy it if your family mixes platforms or you want a long-standing, cross-platform brand. Skip it if everyone carries an iPhone, where AirTag finds more.
pros: One app for the whole family
Ring the tag from your phone
cons: Some features sit behind a plan
products.idealFor: Households that mix iPhone and Android.
products.skipIf: Everyone in your home uses an iPhone.

products.name: Samsung SmartTag2 (2023) Bluetooth + UWB, IP67 Water and Dust Resistant, Findable via App, 1.5 Year Battery Life - Black (International Version)
products.verdict: Bluetooth plus UWB, IP67 protection and a 1.5-year battery.
products.description:
The SmartTag2 adds ultra-wideband to Bluetooth, carries an IP67 rating for water and dust and lists a 1.5-year battery life. It is findable through Samsung's app, and ultra-wideband gives it a more accurate close-range directional search than Bluetooth alone.

It ranks third because it only shines inside Samsung's ecosystem. A Galaxy phone gets a tidy, accurate tag, while other Android phones and iPhones will not get the same experience. The listing also marks it as an International Version, so check that it will work with your region's Samsung services and support before buying.

Pick it if you own a Galaxy phone and want durability. Skip it if you carry any other brand of phone.
pros: IP67 rating handles rain and dust
products.idealFor: Samsung Galaxy owners who want accurate finding.
products.skipIf: You use an iPhone or a non-Samsung phone.

products.name: Life360 Tile Slim - Wallet Finder, Bluetooth Tracker and Item Locator for Luggage Tags, Passports and More. Both iOS and Android Compatible.
products.verdict: A credit card shaped tracker that slides into a wallet or passport.
products.description:
The Tile Slim is shaped like a credit card, so it fits wallets, passport holders and luggage tag sleeves where a bulky disc would not. Like the other Tiles it works on both iOS and Android.

It ranks fourth because it solves the one problem the AirTag and Tile Pro handle badly: a wallet pocket. A thin card goes where a thick tag will not. The tradeoff is that the card format cannot be swapped on a keyring in the same way, and the battery is sealed into the card, so a flat tag means replacing the tracker, not the cell.

Buy it for wallets, passports and thin bags. Skip it if you want one tag for keys, where a thicker model with a hole is simpler.
products.idealFor: Wallet carriers and travelers with passport holders.
products.skipIf: You mainly want to track a set of keys.

products.name: Life360 Tile - Bluetooth Tracker, Keys Finder and Item Locator for Keys, Bags and More. Phone Finder. Both iOS and Android Compatible.
products.verdict: The standard Tile for keys, with a phone finder feature built in.
products.description:
The standard Tile is a key finder and item locator that also lets you ring your phone by pressing the tag. It works with iOS and Android and sits in the under $25 bucket.

It ranks fifth because it covers the same ground as the Tile Pro with less muscle, and Tile does not publish a stated advantage in the listing for it. The double-press phone finder is a lovely everyday trick that AirTag lacks, since it saves a trip to the sofa cushions when you cannot find your phone.

Choose it for a single set of keys or a backpack if you are not an iPhone-only home. Skip it if you want the best range, where the Pro is the better pick.
pros: Press the tag to ring your phone
Simple setup through the Tile app
products.idealFor: Casual users who want a simple key finder on any phone.
products.skipIf: You want the strongest Tile available.

products.name: Air Tags for Android, Air Tags-4 Pack Android, Android Tracker Tags, 2 Year Battery Life, Google Find Trackers for Google'S Find Hub App, IP65 Waterproof
products.verdict: Four Google Find Hub tags with a 2-year battery and IP65 protection.
products.description:
This four-pack is built for Google's Find Hub app on Android, with a 2-year battery listed and an IP65 rating for water and dust. Four tags in one purchase cover keys, a backpack, a laptop bag and a car.

It ranks sixth because an unbranded multi-pack depends heavily on the quality of its app integration and the seller's support, and neither is documented in the listing. IP65 also means resistance to water jets, a step below the IP67 of the Samsung tag. The 2-year battery claim is generous, but is the manufacturer's own.

Buy it if you are on Android and need several tags for the lowest cost per item. Skip it if you have an iPhone, since the tags will not appear in Apple's network.
pros: Four tags for a low total
products.idealFor: Android owners tagging many items on a small budget.
products.skipIf: You carry an iPhone or want a known brand.

products.name: 2 Pack Tracker Tags Finder Apple Find My MFi Certified Waterproof iOS Only
products.verdict: A two-pack that uses Apple Find My, aimed at iPhone owners.
products.description:
This two-pack is described as Apple Find My compatible, MFi certified, waterproof and iOS only. MFi stands for Made for iPhone, a certification that the accessory meets Apple's program requirements for working with its network.

It ranks seventh because it is a third-party alternative to the AirTag with a thin listing and no stated battery life or waterproof rating. The attraction is that it taps the same Find My network at a lower cost per tag. The risk is firmware and support: a third-party tag may differ in alert behavior and in the notices you get about unknown trackers.

Buy it if you are on iPhone and want two tags cheaper than Apple's own. Skip it if you want the polish of Precision Finding.
pros: Uses the Apple Find My network
products.idealFor: iPhone owners who want a cheaper second tag.
products.skipIf: You want Precision Finding or Apple's own support.

products.name: 2 Pack Bluetooth Tracker Works with Apple Find My, Key Finder Locator with Sound, Anti-Lost Device for Wallet Keys iPhone
products.verdict: A two-pack Find My tracker with sound, but with questionable marketing.
products.description:
This two-pack works with Apple Find My, makes a sound to help you find items and is pitched as an anti-lost device for wallets, keys and an iPhone. The listing also calls it a GPS tracking device for kids, pets and luggage.

It ranks last because that GPS claim is misleading. Bluetooth trackers do not contain GPS, and they cannot follow a child or a pet across town; they only report when a nearby phone detects them. Treat any such claim as a reason for caution, and never rely on a tag like this to keep a child safe.

It is fine for finding keys and wallets around the house if you use an iPhone and want the lowest price. Skip it if you are looking for real tracking of people or animals.
pros: Plays a sound to locate items
Two tags for a low price
cons: Limited detail on battery or rating
products.idealFor: iPhone users who want the cheapest pair for keys.
products.skipIf: You want to track a child, a pet or a car.

methodology.description: We compared Apple Find My, Google Find Hub, Samsung's app and the Tile community for how many phones can relay a lost tag.

methodology.description: Listed ratings such as IP65 and IP67 and battery lives of 1.5 and 2 years were weighed as evidence of long-term reliability.

methodology.title: Form factor
methodology.description: Discs, cards and multi-packs were scored for whether they suit keys, wallets, luggage or pets.

methodology.title: Honest marketing
methodology.description: Claims such as GPS tracking were checked against how Bluetooth trackers actually work, within the under $25 bucket.

whatMatters.detail: A tracker only reports a location when a phone on its network passes nearby. Apple Find My is the largest for iPhones, Google Find Hub serves Android and Tile uses its own community. Pick the network that matches the phones around you, since an unsupported tag can only ring when you are within Bluetooth range.

Bluetooth alone tells you roughly how near an item is. Ultra-wideband, as in the SmartTag2, and Precision Finding on the AirTag point you in a direction. If you often lose things inside your home, look for a listing that names UWB or Precision Finding.

IP ratings describe protection against water and dust. IP65 resists splashes and jets, while IP67 handles brief immersion. For keys that live in a jacket or a bag in the rain, aim for at least IP65, and be wary of a vague waterproof label with no rating.

Most round tags use a coin cell that you swap, and the listings here claim 1.5 to 2 years. Card trackers like the Tile Slim seal the battery in. Check whether the cell is replaceable, because a sealed battery makes the tag disposable.

Reputable networks notify you if an unknown tag travels with you. This protection varies across third-party tags. If you use a no-name tracker, understand that safeguards may be weaker, and never use any tracker to follow a person without their consent.

faq.q: Will an AirTag work with my Android phone?
faq.a: No. AirTag setup requires an iPhone or iPad, and Android phones can only detect an unknown tag nearby. Choose a Tile or a Find Hub tracker if you use Android.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying a tracker?
faq.a: Picking by hardware without checking the network. The best tag on the shelf is useless if your phone cannot join its find network. Check compatibility first.

faq.q: Is the Tile Pro worth it over the standard Tile?
faq.a: If you lose keys often or want a more capable tag, yes. The Pro is the stronger of the two, while the standard Tile suffices for a single set of keys at home.

faq.q: How do I set up a tracker?
faq.a: Pull the battery tab, open the app and follow the pairing prompt. Name the tag, such as Keys, and test it by ringing from the app. AirTag pairs with a single tap on iPhone.

faq.q: How do I replace the battery?
faq.a: Most disc tags open with a twist and use a common coin cell. Tile Slim and some card trackers have sealed batteries. Check the listing, since battery lives of 1.5 to 2 years mean a tag may need replacing in the end.

faq.q: Can I track a pet or a child with these?
faq.a: Not reliably. Bluetooth trackers need a nearby phone to report a location and have no GPS. Use a purpose-built GPS pet collar or a child safety device instead.

finalTake: The Apple AirTag (2nd Generation) is the best tracker under $25 for iPhone owners because of the Find My network and Precision Finding. The Tile Pro is the safe answer for mixed households, the Samsung SmartTag2 suits Galaxy owners, and the Android four-pack is the cheapest way to tag many items. Treat any tracker that markets GPS with suspicion, and choose by phone first.
